metadata.title_guess: Accelerated Sparse Recovery with Restarted FISTA

evidence_registry.text: Restarted FISTA reached a relative recovery error of 1.2 × 10^-3 after 200 iterations on the N = 512, K = 50 benchmark.
The restart schedule reduced the number of iterations to reach 10^-3 error by a factor of 1.8 compared with standard FISTA.
The proximal step uses the soft-thresholding operator with a step size of 1/L, where L is the Lipschitz constant of the gradient.
The measurement matrix was drawn from a Gaussian ensemble with unit-column normalization, and measurements contained 30 dB additive white Gaussian noise.
The restart condition triggers when the objective increases relative to the previous iterate.
The method was evaluated on 100 random trials, and the median error is reported.
The acceleration gain decreases when the true support is highly coherent.
Experiments use synthetic signals only; no hardware acquisition or real imaging data were tested.
At a coherence level of 0.8, the saving fell to 9%.
